name: Mosswater Stilts
roofLanguage: Steep dark oak gables, one block up per block in, with a deliberate sag or offset ridge; moss block and moss carpet patches on the lower courses; ragged overhang of 1.
silhouette: Narrow, top-heavy boxes perched 3+ blocks above water on mangrove stilts, upper floors jettied out, ridges kinked, chimneys leaning; joined by sagging boardwalks.
motifs: mangrove log stilts with cross-bracing fences
upper storey jettied 1 block past the lower
ridge line stepped or offset by one block (crooked)
moss carpet and vines creeping up from the waterline
bleached stripped spruce board patches on weather sides
net lofts and drying racks under the eaves
lanterns hung from fence arms over the water
lighting: Sparse warm lanterns hung on fence arms at doors, boardwalk corners and pier ends, one every 6-8 blocks; the hall gets a lantern cluster under its eaves. Keep it dim and foggy.
avoid: perfectly symmetrical facades or dead-straight ridges
buildings sitting directly on the ground or water
bright or clean materials: no white, quartz, polished stone
glass blocks or large window walls
prompt: weathered fishing village on stilts, mossy and crooked
